calls.prompt:
Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Affected areas and owners:
- food-safety: Additives, dyes, labeling, food safety → Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory)
- sourcing: Ingredients from farms, pesticide limits, crop rules → Tom Alvarez (Sourcing)
- sales: Retail channels, SNAP, pricing → Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance)
- operations: Plant safety, labor, trucking fleet → Ben Kowalski (Operations)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-11-13, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-11-13; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.
calls.output:
I found five Federal Register documents from 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-13 that affect Brightside. All five are Critical, because each is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline under 90 days after 2026-11-13.

**1. 2026-22866: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride**
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22866/color-additive-petition-from-the-international-association-of-color-manufacturers-request-to-amend
- **Type and date:** Rule, published November 10, 2026, 91 FR 72410.
- **Key deadline:** Effective January 11, 2027. Comments are due December 12, 2026.
- **Tier:** Critical
- **Owner:** food-safety (Maria Chen)
- **Reason:** FDA removed methylene chloride, trichloroethylene and ethylene dichloride as authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin and turmeric oleoresin. These are common colorants, so they may be in the hot dog, sausage and gummy supply chain.
- **Action:** Ask color suppliers to confirm in writing that none of these solvents are used. Update specifications before January 11, 2027, and decide whether to file comments by December 12.

**2. 2026-22865: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene**
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22865/color-additive-petition-from-environmental-defense-fund-et-al-request-to-amend-the-color-additive
- **Type and date:** Rule, published November 10, 2026, 91 FR 72413.
- **Key deadline:** Same as item 1. The two orders took effect January 11, 2027, and comments are due December 12, 2026. I did not find a separate date for this document.
- **Tier:** Critical
- **Owner:** food-safety (Maria Chen)
- **Reason:** FDA removed the authorized use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. This is a lower-impact item for Brightside. It is relevant mainly to marked produce such as the apples we buy, and to color-additive compliance generally.
- **Action:** Confirm with apple suppliers that none of their fruit-marking inks use methylene chloride. Otherwise, note it for the file.

**3. 2026-22936: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility**
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22936. This is the short link. I only saw the govinfo copy of the document.
- **Type and date:** Proposed rule, published November 10, 2026.
- **Key deadline:** Written comments are due on or before December 10, 2026.
- **Tier:** Critical
- **Owner:** sales (Aisha Grant)
- **Reason:** The proposal would limit categorical eligibility to households that receive TANF assistance. Many of our customers pay with SNAP, so fewer eligible households would reduce demand. USDA estimates the rule would cut federal benefit spending by roughly $44.6 billion over five years.
- **Action:** Model the SNAP-driven sales exposure by retail channel. Decide with trade groups and customers whether to comment by December 10.

**4. 2026-22944: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults**
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22944. This is the short link. I only saw the govinfo PDF. The document number comes from the PDF filename, so please verify it.
- **Type and date:** Proposed rule, published November 10, 2026.
- **Key deadline:** Written comments are due on or before December 10, 2026.
- **Tier:** Critical
- **Owner:** sales (Aisha Grant)
- **Reason:** It would codify USDA's implementation of One Big Beautiful Bill Act changes to the three-month SNAP time limit. That could reduce the number of SNAP participants who shop at our retail customers.
- **Action:** Add to the SNAP demand-risk model alongside item 3. Decide whether to comment by December 10.

**5. 2026-22826: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements**
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22826/pecans-grown-in-the-states-of-alabama-arkansas-arizona-california-florida-georgia-kansas-louisiana
- **Type and date:** Proposed rule by the Agricultural Marketing Service, published 11/09/2026.
- **Key deadline:** Written comments are due by Dec. 9, 2026. That date comes from a trade-press summary, not the Federal Register text I saw.
- **Tier:** Critical
- **Owner:** sourcing (Tom Alvarez)
- **Reason:** The proposal would change sheller membership and nomination on the American Pecan Council, adjust the inter-handler transfer report form, and add late fees and interest on unpaid assessments. It affects our pecan supply chain and any handler obligations we or our shellers have.
- **Action:** Ask pecan shellers and suppliers how the changes affect pricing, assessments and reporting. Confirm whether Brightside is itself a regulated handler, and decide whether to comment by December 9.

**Considered but excluded**
- **Ethephon; Pesticide Tolerances (2026-23120, 11/13):** It sets tolerances only for fig. That is not a crop we buy.
- **Isocycloseram emergency tolerance (2026-23115, 11/13):** It covers sunflower seed only.
- **SNAP stocking-standards 90-day extension (effective Nov. 13):** USDA's website announces it. It gives SNAP authorized retailers 90 more days to meet the stocking standards in the May 2026 final rule. I did not find a Federal Register document for it in the window. The underlying May final rule is 2026-09137, published in May and outside the window. It lists snack bars as accessory foods that don't count as staples, which is worth checking for our products.
- **FMCSA 11/09 driver exemption notice (epilepsy and seizure disorders):** The FMCSA listing shows it as a notice dated 11/09/2026. It concerns individual drivers' exemption applications, not our fleet's rules.

My searches may not have caught every document in the window. I found no qualifying OSHA, FSIS or apple-marketing-order documents, but I can't rule them out.

items.action: Ask color suppliers to confirm in writing that none of these solvents are used, update specifications before 2027-01-11, and decide whether to file comments by 2026-12-12.

items.title: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene
items.reason: Rule (91 FR 72413, published 2026-11-10): FDA removed the authorized use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. Lower impact for Brightside, relevant mainly to marked produce such as the apples we buy and to color-additive compliance generally. Dates are the same as the companion order (effective 2027-01-11, comments due 2026-12-12); no separate date was found for this document.
items.action: Confirm with apple suppliers that none of their fruit-marking inks use methylene chloride; otherwise note it for the file.

items.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility
items.reason: Proposed rule (published 2026-11-10) would limit categorical eligibility to households receiving TANF assistance. Many of our customers pay with SNAP, so fewer eligible households would reduce demand; USDA estimates federal benefit spending would fall by roughly $44.6 billion over five years. Only the govinfo copy was seen; the URL is the short link.
items.action: Model the SNAP-driven sales exposure by retail channel, and decide with trade groups and customers whether to comment by 2026-12-10.

items.title: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults
items.reason: Proposed rule (published 2026-11-10) would codify USDA's implementation of One Big Beautiful Bill Act changes to the three-month SNAP time limit, which could reduce the number of SNAP participants shopping at our retail customers. Only the govinfo PDF was seen; the document number comes from the PDF filename and needs verification; the URL is the short link.
items.action: Verify the document number, add to the SNAP demand-risk model alongside 2026-22936, and decide whether to comment by 2026-12-10.

items.title: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements
items.reason: Agricultural Marketing Service proposed rule (published 2026-11-09) would change sheller membership and nomination on the American Pecan Council, adjust the inter-handler transfer report form, and add late fees and interest on unpaid assessments, affecting our pecan supply chain and any handler obligations we or our shellers have. The comment date of 2026-12-09 comes from a trade-press summary, not the Federal Register text seen.
items.action: Ask pecan shellers and suppliers how the changes affect pricing, assessments and reporting, confirm whether Brightside is itself a regulated handler, verify the comment deadline, and decide whether to comment by 2026-12-09.
